newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Jews defend Romania govt on assets return policy.
newsitem.headline: Jews defend Romania govt on assets return policy.

text.p: Romanian Jewish community leaders defended the centrist government on Tuesday against accusations that it stalled the return of assets seized from Jews by World War Two fascists and later by Communists.
"The government has already returned five community properties, and others will follow," Nicolae Cajal, head of the Federation of Jewish communities, told a news conference.

Cajal protested against last week's move by an influential group leading Jewish restitution efforts to criticise Romania, Poland and the Czech Republic as countries slow to return assets confiscated from Jews during the Nazi Holocaust.

"Romania's present government and its president back full restitution of the properties seized from all ethnic groups," said Cajal, whose federation represents Romania's 14,000 Jews, all that remain of a pre-war community of 800,000.

Cajal said he would protest to the World Jewish Restitution Organisation (WJRO), an Israel-based umbrella group of Jewish organisations which presses for the return of Jewish assets confiscated by the Nazis or by post-war communist regimes.

One of the WJRO's leading members, the World Jewish Congress, has led efforts to press Swiss authorities for compensation for Holocaust survivors whose pre-war savings were deposited in Swiss bank accounts or looted by the Nazis.

A WJRO executive said his group last week singled out Hungary for praise in returning Jewish property. But he denied media reports the WJRO would try to lobby the U.S. Senate to hinder Polish, Czech and Romanian bids for NATO membership.
"We will do our utmost to support Hungary, which has complied with all restitution promises," WJRO vice-chairman Naphtali Lavie told Reuters by telephone from Jerusalem.
"The Czechs, Poles and Romanians have not complied with their promises. We won't intervene in their favour, but that doesn't mean blocking their bids."

On Thursday, Romania's parliament, dominated by centrists who ousted leftists in elections last November, is expected to endorse a government order to return five Jewish properties, including a Bucharest theatre, a school and a ritual bath.
Foreign Minister Adrian Severin is also due to meet WJRO leaders during a visit to Israel on Sunday.
Later this week, Romania will set up a foundation called Caritas, run by WRJO and local Jewish leaders, to administer returned Jewish community assets, Cajal said.
Half of Romania's 800,000 Jews died in Nazi death camps. Of the survivors, 320,000 left for Israel in the Communist era.
